bullets.title: META: Cloud compute launch triggers AI crowding unwind; Zuckerberg admits AI behind schedule
bullets.body: META launched a new cloud infrastructure business to sell external compute and AI model access, which JPM views as supportive of sustained capex and monetization, but which also triggered profit-taking across AI tech with Global Memory -15% and Broad AI -7.5% on the week. Separately, Zuckerberg acknowledged in an internal town hall that Meta's AI agent development and internal reorganization are tracking behind initial expectations. META also launched 'Pocket,' a social app with vibe-coded mini games, seen as competitive pressure on RBLX.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 17 production cut 15%; memory supplier talks face national security pushback
bullets.body: Apple cut iPhone 17 production by ~15% as demand normalizes, with iPhone 18 also expected to see a tepid reception. AAPL is reportedly in talks to source memory chips from Chinese suppliers on the Pentagon blacklist and is lobbying the White House for political cover; the situation creates headline/regulatory risk. AAPL gained +8.8% on the week despite these overhangs.

bullets.title: TSLA: Q2 deliveries 480K+, up 34% q/q and 25% y/y, beat ~406K consensus
bullets.body: Tesla delivered 480K+ vehicles in Q2, up 34% sequentially and 25% year-over-year, well above the ~406K consensus estimate, though expectations were flagged as elevated heading into the print.

bullets.title: SMCI: Taiwan office raided in AI chip-smuggling investigation; stock -11.1%
bullets.body: Taiwanese authorities raided Supermicro's office in connection with an AI chip-smuggling investigation, sending shares down 11.1% on the week. The probe is seen as a brand and regulatory risk; the item notes Nvidia is backstopping younger cloud providers in exchange for revenue share, which could benefit Dell and SMCI as HPC providers separately.

bullets.title: ADBE upgraded to Buy at HSBC; AI disruption fears overdone
bullets.body: HSBC upgraded Adobe to Buy from Hold, arguing that AI disruption fears are overdone with no evidence of market share loss to date.

bullets.title: PLTR upgraded to Buy at DA Davidson on valuation and competitive moat
bullets.body: DA Davidson upgraded Palantir to Buy from Neutral, citing valuation and competitive advantages as the key drivers.

bullets.title: Wolfe upgrades SaaS/security; top longs MDB, DDOG, SNOW, NOW, PANW
bullets.body: Wolfe's June 'Manic Monthly' calls MDB an alpha pick on 30%+ Atlas growth and re-rating potential; DDOG early channel checks described as 'great' with GPU consumption upside; SNOW benefiting from AI-driven usage growth; NOW an 'underappreciated long-term AI winner' with positive Q2 checks; PANW the biggest beneficiary of the Mythos security trade (+25% in June). All-SaaS index trades at 5.3x FY+2 EV/Sales vs. All-Security at 8.3x. IGV is down 14.3% YTD.

bullets.title: Mag 7 / AI Tech momentum unwind: HFs sold at -2z to -3z; Tech Momentum worst month since early 2000s
bullets.body: MS QDS reports Tech Momentum (MSZZTMTM) down 20% MTD and 11% on Friday alone — the worst month since the early 2000s. HFs were net sellers of Mag 7 and Software at -2z each in June, with positioning falling to the 16th and 11th percentiles respectively. AI Tech Beneficiaries were sold ~3z amounts with Thursday the largest single net-reduction day. HF gross leverage peaked at the 98th percentile on a 5-year basis but early de-grossing has begun; JPM seasonality points to more into late July.

bullets.title: ORLY: Mixed reaction to potential $10B+ GPC auto acquisition; UBS Buy, Mizuho skeptical
bullets.body: Bloomberg reported ORLY is pursuing a cash bid for GPC's auto parts arm, valued at $10B+ globally (76 distribution centers, ~6,800 stores), sending ORLY shares down ~3%. UBS maintains Buy at $120 PT (~32x CY'27 EPS), citing geographic diversification and synergy potential, but flags 60% store overlap and likely FTC scrutiny. Mizuho is skeptical, noting GPC's sub-10% EBITDA margins vs. ORLY's consistent 20%+, and prefers smaller tuck-in acquisitions.

bullets.title: HOOD +19.8% on perpetual futures launch; CEO discusses UK expansion
bullets.body: Robinhood surged 19.8% on the week after launching perpetual futures on commodities and ETFs, with the CEO also commenting on plans for UK market expansion.

bullets.title: AMZN: Project Kuiper launches 29 satellites to begin broadband service by end of 2026
bullets.body: Amazon launched 29 satellites via an Atlas V rocket on July 2, initiating its Project Kuiper constellation with commercial broadband service expected to begin later this year, directly competing with SpaceX's Starlink.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Spinoff of NBCUniversal and Sky viewed positively; JPM recommends short on CMCSA bonds
bullets.body: CMCSA gained +2.7% on the week on NBCUniversal and Sky spinoff plans. On the credit side, JPM recommends shorting CMCSA 5.30% '35 bonds, noting spreads are trading tight relative to US telecom peers following the split announcement.

bullets.title: FICO: Dominates GSE mortgage market at 99.1% share; VantageScore reaches only 90bps in first material month
bullets.body: FICO backed $61.2B of $61.8B in GSE fixed-rate mortgages (99.1% share) in June 2026 data. VantageScore 4.0 reached $556M (90bps) in its first month of material volume, concentrated almost entirely at United Wholesale Mortgage (87% of VantageScore use), suggesting no near-term threat to FICO's dominance.

bullets.title: WYNN: UBS maintains Buy/$146 PT; cuts Q2 Vegas/Boston estimates on June softness
bullets.body: UBS trims Q2 Vegas revenue to $637M (flat YoY) and EBITDA to $213M (-9% YoY) on lower airlift, with Harry Reid airport traffic down 7-8% YoY. Boston Q2 EBITDA cut to $54M from $57M. Macau GGR was down 12% YoY in June due to World Cup, but UBS expects rebound in August; Al Marjan Island opening pushed to late 2027. Buy and $146 PT unchanged.

bullets.title: SHOP +5.1% on Canadian tape; HUT -17.5% hit by META cloud/compute narrative
bullets.body: Shopify gained +5.1% to C$170.56 in mid-afternoon Canadian trading. Hut 8 Mining fell 17.5% to C$135.17, consistent with the broader Bitcoin miner selloff (miners down >20%) triggered by skepticism around compute scarcity following META's cloud launch.

bullets.title: RBLX: Competitive pressure from META's 'Pocket' mini-games app flagged
bullets.body: META is rolling out a new app called Pocket featuring a social feed of vibe-coded mini games, seen as a direct competitive threat to Roblox's core user engagement model. RBLX shares were down on the news.

bullets.title: NFLX, ROKU, CMCSA, FOXA: JPM Media M&A Webinar scheduled July 6
bullets.body: JPMorgan is hosting a Media M&A Webinar on July 6 at 10am ET covering CMCSA, NFLX, ROKU, FOXA and others — potentially relevant ahead of any further spinoff or deal news.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler options overlay: 6-month IV at multiyear highs; upside calls cheaply skewed vs ATM
bullets.body: 22V Research notes META, AMZN, and MSFT 6-month implied volatility is at multiyear highs with upside calls richly skewed versus ATM options, creating a low-cost overlay entry point for long exposure into H2 hyperscaler rebound.

bullets.title: Soft June payrolls (57K vs. 110K est.) cement Fed on hold; semi/memory crowding continues to unwind
bullets.body: June nonfarm payrolls came in at just 57K vs. 110K consensus, with prior months revised down 74K; unemployment fell to 4.2% on lower participation (61.5%, lowest since March 2021). Fed rate hike odds fell to ~17% for July. Morgan Stanley and 22V both expect Fed on hold through 2026. Semis (SOX -4.4% for week) and memory continued to unwind amid AI capex scrutiny, with SK Hynix and Micron carrying the highest short gamma (-$16B/1% move).
